category_title: Young children with persistent challenging behaviors and communication delays
minimal_context: Kayden and his mother are at home in the evening, and she prompts him to start getting ready for bed.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Kayden, it is time to start to get ready for bed.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Come on, we need to get ready for bed now.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Kayden, it is time to start to get ready for bed.

STUDENT: (Starts crying) No!

TUTOR: Come on, we need to get ready for bed now.

STUDENT: (Cries louder)

TUTOR: Stop crying and let's go.

STUDENT: (Screams and starts hitting)

task.content: Start to get ready for bed

context.materials: Pajamas, favorite book, low-energy games, puzzle

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: The prompt from mom for Kayden to start to get ready for bed
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Some amount of screaming, crying, and/or hitting will likely occur
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Screaming and hitting usually result in more attention from mom

behavior_patterns.condition: After the prompt to get ready for bed, at some point between delivery of the prompt and Kayden actually falling asleep
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Seeking attention in the form of repeated prompts, reprimands, and mom lying down in bed with him
